conventions.convention: Assume Countable Choice for the normalized torus measure convention. The torus is (R/LZ)^d, d ∈ {1,2,3}, with probability measure dμ_L = L^(-d) dx. Convolution uses volume measure, equivalently L^d dμ_L.

K is nonnegative, smooth, supported in a compact subset of the open unit ball, and has Euclidean integral one; 0 < ℓ < L/2. Fields being filtered have finitely many real components and smooth periodic spatial slices.

The tensor product has components (u⊗v)_ij = u_i v_j, the velocity gradient has components ∂_j v_i, and A:B is the sum of componentwise products. Forward transfer is Π_ℓ = −τ_ℓ:∇ū_ℓ; positivity of covariance does not imply positivity of transfer.

The covariance conclusion requires no evolution equation. The momentum and energy conclusions additionally assume the stated smooth incompressible equation, constant ν > 0, and smooth pressure and forcing; pressure and forcing are per unit mass.

The Hölder estimate assumes the displayed increment bound with 0 < α < 1. Its time-integrated conclusion additionally requires Lebesgue measurability and integrability of A^3; it asserts no decay at α = 1/3.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated nonnegative smooth compactly supported unit-mass kernel and 0 < ℓ < L/2, define the periodized convolution filter, τ_ℓ = overline(u⊗u)_ℓ − ū_ℓ⊗ū_ℓ, and Π_ℓ = −τ_ℓ:∇ū_ℓ.

Under Countable Choice and the stated kernel and torus hypotheses, the periodized kernel is smooth, nonnegative, periodic, and has volume integral one. Filtering equals the Euclidean integral of K(s)q(x−ℓs,t), commutes with the stated spatial and time derivatives under the specified regularity, and has finite moments M_γ and N_γ for γ > 0.

Under the stated positive-filter hypotheses and u ∈ C^1(I;C^∞), τ_ℓ equals the increment second moment minus the tensor square of the increment mean and is symmetric positive semidefinite. Under the additional smooth incompressible equation with constant ν > 0, the filtered momentum equation and the stated local and integrated resolved-energy balances hold, with +τ_ℓ:∇ū_ℓ on the energy right-hand side and no asserted sign for Π_ℓ.

Under the stated regularity, positive-filter hypotheses, and increment bound |u(x−ℓs,t)−u(x,t)| ≤ A(t)ℓ^α|s|^α for s in supp K and 0 < α < 1, |Π_ℓ(x,t)| ≤ d²(M_(2α)+M_α²)N_α A(t)^3 ℓ^(3α−1). The corresponding supremum-in-space time integral obeys the displayed bound when A^3 is Lebesgue integrable on J.

concerns.concern: The convolution is written as an integral of G_ℓ(r)q(x−r) with differential dx, although x is the free evaluation variable and r is the integration variable. The equivalent expression using dμ_L(r) makes the intended definition clear. Use dr consistently in the volume-measure expression. The same notation recurs in the Statements of lem-fd-periodic-filter-normalization-and-commutation, thm-fd-filtered-covariance-energy, and thm-fd-holder-energy-transfer-bound.

seams_checked.note: Checked def-fd-periodic-fourier-sobolev-spaces against its normalized unit-torus suppliers. Rescaling x = Ly and ξ = 2πy preserves the probability-measure convention; convolution separately uses volume measure with the explicit L^d conversion. Countable Choice is retained. No Sobolev embedding or product estimate is silently imported.

Read post-fd-eddy-viscosity-closure and pthm-fd-eddy-closure-resolved-dissipation. They preserve the positive-filter definition, spatial derivative commutation, gradient convention, and transfer sign. The exact energy theorem is invoked only with the additional ν > 0 and smooth-pressure conditions. Modeled stress is explicitly distinguished from exact covariance, so modeled nonnegative transfer is not attributed to the exact stress.
